description: A stereo phaser of twelve or twenty four stages, of second or fourth order, with its own modulating oscillator and a jack for modulating it from elsewhere

params.text: Sets the speed of the modulating oscillator
Sets how far the modulating oscillator sweeps the phaser, -1 to +1, running the sweep backwards at negative settings
Sets the resonance of the phasing stages, 0 to 1
Sets the depth of the phasing effect, 0 to 0.8
Sets the width of the band the phasing works over, inside the range from 20Hz to 10kHz
Sets the frequency at the middle of the phasing band, inside the range from 20Hz to 10kHz
Chooses twelve or twenty four phasing stages
Chooses a second order or a fourth order filter in each stage
Chooses the shape of the modulating oscillator: sine, triangle, saw or square
Switches the phaser out of the signal path, passing the inputs through

inputs.text: The left side of the signal into the phaser
A signal that sweeps the phaser in place of its own modulating oscillator
A voltage added to the modulation speed
A voltage added to the modulation depth
A voltage added to the resonance
A voltage added to the phasing depth
A voltage added to the bandwidth
A voltage added to the centre frequency
The right side of the signal into the phaser
A trigger switches the phaser out of the path and back in

outputs.text: The left side of the phased signal
The right side of the phased signal
